bottom_line.text: Laparoscopic repair reduces chronic postoperative pain compared with Lichtenstein repair [90000001; 90000002; 90000003]. The absolute benefit is mainly in mild pain [90000004]. One long-term trial found no difference at about 8 years [90000007].
bottom_line.certainty_reason: Consistent direction across overlapping meta-analyses, but pain definitions vary and trials are open-label.

outcomes.effect_text: Laparoscopic repair roughly halves to thirds the risk of any chronic groin pain compared with Lichtenstein. TEP vs Lichtenstein: RR 0.38 (95% CI 0.28-0.51) across 27 RCTs with 7,658 patients [90000001]. At 5 years: 9.4% with TEP vs 18.8% with Lichtenstein (P < 0.001) [90000004]. The exception is TEPLICH at about 8 years: 7.6% with TEP vs 6.7% with Lichtenstein [90000007].
outcomes.why: Consistent direction and large pooled effects; downgraded because one long-term trial found no difference and pain definitions vary.

outcomes.effect_text: The absolute difference is much smaller for pain that matters: 1.9% with TEP vs 3.5% with Lichtenstein at 5 years (P = 0.092) [90000004].

outcomes.effect_text: There is no overall difference in recurrence: RR 1.03 (95% CI 0.62-1.72) [90000001]. The Swedish trial found 3.5% with TEP vs 1.2% with Lichtenstein [90000005].
outcomes.why: Pooled estimate is imprecise; one trial's excess was surgeon-specific.

outcomes.effect_text: Operative costs were higher for TEP but total costs were comparable; no figures in the abstract [90000006].
outcomes.why: A single trial from a European setting.

outcomes.effect_text: Wound infection is less frequent after laparoscopic repair: RR 0.48 (95% CI 0.31-0.75) [90000001].
outcomes.why: Few events in single trials; consistent pooled effect.

conflicts.text: TEPLICH found no difference in pain at about 8 years [90000007], unlike the pooled trials [90000001]; longer follow-up and a stricter pain definition may explain it.

applicability.case_mix: Mostly primary unilateral hernias in men [90000001].

at_a_glance:
Laparoscopic repair causes less chronic pain than Lichtenstein repair [90000001; 90000002].
- Chronic pain: RR 0.38 with TEP vs Lichtenstein [90000001]
- Chronic pain at 5 years: 9.4% with TEP vs 18.8% with Lichtenstein [90000004]
- Recurrence: RR 1.03, no difference [90000001]
Main caveat: pain definitions vary and trials are open-label.
clinical_practice:
Default choice: Offer TEP or TAPP when a surgeon experienced in it is available [90000001; 90000002]. Lichtenstein remains a sound repair when laparoscopic expertise is lacking [90000005].
Who may benefit: Patients most concerned about chronic pain [90000004].
Counselling: Fewer people have lasting groin pain after keyhole repair; recurrence is similar [90000001].
Cost per case: not known
notable_findings:
- One surgeon's results raised the TEP recurrence rate in the Swedish trial [90000005].
- The two meta-analyses share many trials, so they are not independent evidence [90000001; 90000002].
- The longest follow-up found no difference in pain [90000007].
